clue.text: On the ship of love, in a poet's embrace

indicators.note: the poet's embrace wraps round the love, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bard is a poet
love is nil in tennis scoring, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic image of love held tight in a poet's arms, perhaps on a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a poet's embrace' puts O inside A BARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something on board a vessel is said to be there, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dressing up seaman having alarming vices when drunk

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for seaman is written bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor with frightening vices, much the worse for drink, is dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AB into BA; 'drunk' rearranges ALARMING VICES into LSAMICVINEGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark Italian vinegar is commonly used as a salad dressing, so the dressing is an example.

clue.text: In Part B: Rutherford's primitive form of expression

indicators.note: In says the letters sit within the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A physics textbook's second section discusses Ernest Rutherford's primitive way of expressing his ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Rutherford, the physicist, is just cover for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Art brut, raw art made by untrained outsiders, is a deliberately primitive mode of artistic expression.

clue.text: Succulent cryptic clue is: 'I'd brought round ring'

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are brought round the ring, enclosing it
cryptic means obscured or puzzling, so these words are jumbled before use

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a tasty cryptic clue whose words were wrapped round a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUE IS I'D into DELICIUS; 'brought round' wraps that round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent dish is juicy and tasty, which is what a delicious one is.

clue.text: Elton, holding pants back to front to show spread

indicators.note: the name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Ben Elton is a British comedian and writer, so Elton is Ben

indicators.note: the last letter of the trousers word is brought round to the front

parts.note: pants are trousers, and trews are tartan trousers

explanation.surface: Elton holds his trousers on backwards in a comic display.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Elton is a British comedian, and trews are Scottish tartan trousers; 'pants' is the British word for underwear or, as here, trousers generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestrewn is an old past participle meaning scattered or strewn about, a synonym for spread.

clue.text: Save time: break off edge of plank

parts.note: save as in 'all save one' means but, except
to break off is to end

explanation.surface: A carpenter is told to save time by snapping off the edge of the plank.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt end is the thicker or squared-off end of a timber, the end edge of a board.

clue.text: Hits that come in twos

definitions.meaning: punches or blows, as in landing a few on someone
foot garments worn and sold in pairs

explanation.surface: A one-two punch, or hit records that arrive as doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means strikes hard; as a noun the garments always come as a pair.

clue.text: No dream property would cramp one

indicators.note: to cramp is to confine, so the property squeezes the one inside itself

parts.note: realty is real estate, property in land and buildings
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dream home that would be cramped for even a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would cramp' puts I inside REALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: What is actual and not imagined is the opposite of a dream, a definition by contrast.

clue.text: Fill in catchword, 'Wicked!' — it'll make you feel more cool

definitions.text: it'll make you feel more cool

indicators.note: wicked here has its sense of twisted or perverse, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A teenager is told to fill in a trendy catchword like 'Wicked!' to sound cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked!' rearranges FILL IN CATCHWORD. 'Cool' looks like teen slang praise; it means cold.
explanation.definitionFit: This weather measure expresses how much colder the air feels on skin because of wind.

clue.text: Armour section (rented) that's essential for a clot

parts.note: a plate is a piece of plate armour
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A piece of armour hired out, which turns out to be vital for a clot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clot' looks like an insult for a fool; here it is a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny blood cells clump together to form clots, so they are essential to clotting.

clue.text: Old lady gives up a lot of money for carbon fissure

indicators.note: gives up one thing for another means it is swapped out for the replacement

parts.note: an old lady is a granny
G is a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An elderly woman sacrifices a fortune for some carbon, perhaps a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives up ... for' replaces G in GRANNY with C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small crack or narrow opening, as in nook and cranny, so a synonym.

clue.text: See 22
Castle Cheese pics doctored?

indicators.note: doctored pictures are tampered with, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether photos of cheese from a castle have been faked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctored' rearranges CHEESE PICS. 'Castle' looks like a building; it is the rook.
explanation.definitionFit: The castle is another name for the rook, one of the pieces used on the board in chess.

clue.text: Just the top of roast covered with gravy browning here?

definitions.text: Just the top of roast covered with gravy browning here?

indicators.note: the letter is covered by the gravy product, sitting inside it

parts.note: Bisto is a British brand of gravy browning powder

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A diner gets only a sliver of roast drowned in gravy and wonders if that's the place's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the top of' takes R from roast; 'covered with' puts it inside BISTO, a British gravy powder brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, modest restaurant is a likely place to be served roast with gravy, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: That of one who didn't come clean?

definitions.text: That of one who didn't come clean?

parts.words: That of one who didn't come clean?
parts.note: not coming clean means telling a falsehood, and also staying grubby; a golfer's ball can rest unclean in the ground too

explanation.surface: A question about the habits of someone who never confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, someone who stayed unwashed; really an untruth told shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A grubby falsehood is the typical fib of someone refusing to confess, the idiom for coming clean.

clue.text: Repeat sentence about inmate

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a convict is a prison inmate

explanation.surface: A judge hands down a second sentence concerning a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence someone again for a crime is to find them guilty once more, a verbal equivalent.

clue.text: Spacewalking scene change, then fade out

parts.note: EVA, extravehicular activity, is the technical term for a spacewalk

indicators.note: change asks for the letters of the following word to be put in another order

explanation.surface: A film direction: a spacewalk shot, a scene change, then fade out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SCENE into NESCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to vanish gradually like vapour, a literary synonym for fading away.

clue.text: At present partly within affluent city

indicators.note: only part of the first word, its last letter, goes within the second word

parts.note: at present means now
affluent means rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy city is currently partly enclosed, perhaps by walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter of the 'at present' word moves; the rest stays in front, which is what 'partly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in eastern England, the county town of Norfolk; the clue simply names it as an example.

clue.text: Food involved in Jedi blessing

indicators.note: involved in means the letters are wrapped up inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Star Wars knight blessing a meal before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fit to eat are foodstuffs, so the plural noun matches food in sense.

clue.text: Pod's cold — not like Norfolk, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the letters built are only how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: C, the tap abbreviation for cold, then HILLY, since Norfolk, an English county, is famously flat

explanation.surface: A seed pod complains of the cold and the lack of hills in flat Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: C + HILLY gives CHILLY, which sounds like the spelt answer. Norfolk is an eastern English county known for being flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot pepper is the pod of a capsicum plant, so a pod is a fair description.

clue.text: How, in USA, change might be presented vocally as anger

indicators.note: vocally means spoken out, so we need a phrase that sounds like the letters entered

parts.words: How, in USA, change might be presented
parts.note: American small change comes in cents, so it is given in cents

explanation.surface: A musing on how American coins might be handed over, and why that provokes rage.
explanation.walkthrough: IN CENTS, said out, matches the verb meaning to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, so it is a verb synonym for anger.

clue.text: Violation accepted ahead of French battle

parts.note: something accepted is in, in fashion or admitted
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: A breach of rules was tolerated just before a French battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach of a rule or law, a direct synonym.

clue.text: 'Choc', a material involved in making upmarket attire

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together and used in making something new

explanation.surface: Chocolate is woven into a fabric used for a luxury garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in making' rearranges CHOC A MATERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat made from the soft fur of a desert animal is a classic smart, expensive garment.

clue.text: See 22
Not all frottage is mean form of discrimination

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An art critic claims frottage, rubbing over textures, is a stingy technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice against people because of how old they are is a recognised kind of discrimination.

clue.text: Garland & Bishop fool the last great mathematician

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a nit is a nitwit, a fool
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A list of items, a garland and a bishop, ends with the latest in a line of great mathematicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Leibniz is more usual; this older spelling with T is also accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Gottfried Leibniz co-invented calculus, a towering figure in mathematics.

clue.text: Flaw in insignia, which should not be part of a straitjacket

definitions.text: which should not be part of a straitjacket

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: arms are heraldic insignia, a coat of arms
a hole is a flaw or defect

explanation.surface: A defect in a badge that a maker of restraint jackets must avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: A straitjacket's sleeves are closed and bound, so the wearer's limbs are not free to come through.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings for the limbs to come through would defeat the purpose of a restraining garment.

clue.text: Possible explanation from politician, full of gas

indicators.note: the politician is full of the gas, holding it inside

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: A windbag politician offers an explanation that may or may not hold up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of gas' looks like a jibe at a windbag; the gas is helium. A Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed account of why something happens, which may or may not be right.
